It’s old footage featured in a 2020 documentary, and Dolly’s not singing in it; instead, she’s reading. “She pulled and she tugged. ‘I think I can! I think I can!’ she said”—and of course it’s The Little Engine That Could , the classic folktale made famous by Arnold “Watty Piper” Munk. Then Dolly turns to the kids huddled around her and says, “Would you help me? All of you, help me!” and she chants with them: “I think I can! I think I can!” Here is the thing about Dolly Parton: That woman understood the job she had been given to do, and she did it gladly. Others are not so lucky The Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community sits off state Route 170, on the edge of East Palestine, Ohio, a town most Americans only learned about because a train derailed there in February 2023 and released toxic chemicals into the creek . I grew up in a trailer park like this one, and know the sights. The grid of aluminum boxes in rows. Skirting the color of old teeth, some of it buckled, some patched with a piece of lattice. The window units huff and puff in August, dripping dark condensation on to the gravel. I’m sure there were drugs on my street. I’m sure somebody was selling sex. I never saw it.
